title: Five new implementer-authored success toasts ship em-dashes — violating the module's own documented toast rule and the 2026-08-05 user ruling (RT em-dash ban), and the known pin gap means CI will not catch them
evidence: copy.gleam:874 "Reference started — the invite goes out now."; :878 "Reference re-enabled — it's back in the queue."; :880 "You're handling this one — automated messages stopped."; :882 "Details saved — the invitation is on its way again."; :884 "Referee substituted — the new invitation is on its way." — all five use U+2014. copy.gleam's own module header (line 12) documents the rule: "Toasts are one or two sentences (sentence breaks, never em-dashes)." The 2026-08-05 user ruling pinned in client/test/copy_test.gleam:308 (no_em_dash_test) states "no em-dash may appear in any landlord-facing copy string" — but the test only iterates copy.toast(code, ctx)/copy.page(code, ctx) outputs (for_each_copy, copy_test.gleam:296-303), so these constants bypass it (the known pin gap). The UX spec fixes no toast copy for start/skip/re-enable/take-over/correct/substitute (grep of the UX spec: the only fixed toast is the export toast at §7.6/§10.3, "Attempt log copied — paste it into your records or a message.", which the PR's own spec artifact explicitly defers to RC4.4), so these strings are implementer-authored, not spec-verbatim — the exact case lens-guard 9 flags: "An em-dash ADDED by the implementer where the spec has none, or in implementer-authored strings, is a defect."
detail: AC7 of the acceptance lens (COPY VERBATIM + RT em-dash ban) and the round briefing's legitimate-findings list ("An em-dash in user-facing copy ... a real defect") are violated by the new toasts themselves, independent of the pre-existing pin-gap intake warning. The spec's own refcheck strings that carry em-dashes (refcheck_subline_in_flight, refcheck_state_unreachable, refcheck_explainer_body, signals) are verbatim from the UX spec; these five toasts have no spec source. Because no_em_dash_test does not scan the refcheck_* constants, the em-dashes will reach production landlords unchecked. Fix is trivial: sentence-break rewrites (e.g. "Reference started. The invite goes out now."), matching refcheck_toast_skipped's own dash-free style.
recommended_fix: Rewrite the five toasts with sentence breaks instead of em-dashes (the module doc's prescribed form), e.g. "Reference started. The invite goes out now." / "Reference re-enabled. It's back in the queue." / "You're handling this one. Automated messages stopped." / "Details saved. The invitation is on its way again." / "Referee substituted. The new invitation is on its way."

title: Take-over inline confirm body is not §7.7 verbatim despite the code comment and the PR spec both claiming "§7.7 verbatim" — the referee's name is dropped from the sentence and "he" becomes "they"
evidence: UX §7.7 fixes the confirm verbatim: "Take over this reference yourself? / Automated messages stop, and Colm's details + the attempt log are yours. If he completes the form anyway, it still shows up here." (and UX §10.3 copy deck: "Warm-handoff confirm | §7.7, verbatim"). Implemented body (copy.gleam:824): "Automated messages stop, and the referee's details + the attempt log are yours. If they complete the form anyway, it still shows up here." — "Colm's" → "the referee's" (the name placeholder is removed from the sentence; the name is instead rendered as a separate muted text line under the body) and "he" → "they". The comment above the constant claims "§7.7 take-over inline confirm (verbatim heading + body)" and the PR's own spec artifact (spec-rc4-3-row-actions.md, item 10: "Take over: inline confirm (§7.7 verbatim)"; item 12 "all new strings verbatim from §7.4 ... §7.7") claims verbatim for this string.
detail: AC2 ("the §7.7 inline confirmation renders") and acceptance lens point 7 (COPY VERBATIM — the load-bearing invariant) are not met byte-for-byte. The gender-neutral "he"→"they" change follows the rc4-2 W5 spirit, but the PR spec sanctions gender-neutral copy ONLY for the start-confirm ("start-confirm is gender-neutral per the rc4-2 W5 ruling" — and indeed refcheck_start_confirm at copy.gleam:811 is annotated that way), not for the take-over body; the additional restructuring (name removed from the sentence, "Colm's details" → "the referee's details") is not a gender change at all. The claim of verbatim in both the code comment and the PR spec makes this an undisclosed deviation. The rendered confirm still shows the referee's name on its own line, so the information is preserved — but the string itself is not the specified copy.
recommended_fix: Either restore the §7.7 wording with the name interpolated ("Automated messages stop, and {name}'s details + the attempt log are yours. If they complete the form anyway, it still shows up here." — keeping the W5-style gender-neutral pronoun if desired) or explicitly document the deviation in the PR spec and the copy comment instead of claiming "verbatim".

title: New RC4.3 panel state does NOT reset on route change although model.gleam documents "All reset on route change (they are per-application surfaces)"
location: client/src/model.gleam:370-377 (field docs + reset claim); client/src/client.gleam:657-670 (BrowserChangedUrl ApplicationDetail branch)
evidence: model.gleam:373-374: "All reset on route change (they are per-application surfaces)" — but the BrowserChangedUrl ApplicationDetail branch (client.gleam:657-670) resets only refcheck_expanded: set.new() (:666) and refcheck_explainer_open: False (:667). refcheck_menu_open, refcheck_confirm, refcheck_edit and refcheck_action_inflight are touched only by the RC4.3 action handlers (client.gleam:3306-3541) — never by any navigation path. The client tests pin route-change reset only for the RC4.2 fields (client_test.gleam refcheck_route_change_resets_expanded_rows_test); no test covers the four new fields.
detail: Impact is mostly masked because the renderer scopes menu/confirm/edit by reference_call_id (pending_confirm, edit call-id matching — pinned by confirm_is_scoped_to_its_call_test), and call ids are unique per application, so the stale state does not leak onto a different applicant's rows. The visible cases are navigation-dependent: leaving an application with the §8.3 edit-trio open (or the ⋯ menu open) and returning to the SAME application re-renders the stale surface (e.g. the substitute edit form still open over a row the refetch may have replaced), and refcheck_action_inflight can linger after navigation if a response never arrives. Low severity, but the code contradicts its own documented contract.
recommended_fix: Reset refcheck_menu_open: None, refcheck_confirm: None, refcheck_edit: None, refcheck_action_inflight: set.new() alongside refcheck_expanded in the BrowserChangedUrl ApplicationDetail branch (and add the assertion to the existing route-change reset test).

title: New attempt-log clipboard export composes lines with " — " joins — the round briefing's "timeline ` — ` joins" defect category — though consistent with §7.6's timeline format and the RC4.2 on-screen timeline
evidence: build_attempt_log_text joins each line as attempt.at <> " — " <> attempt.channel <> " — " <> attempt.outcome, producing a landlord-facing clipboard artifact ("Reference: {name}\nState: {status}\n..."). The round briefing's legitimate-findings list states "An em-dash in user-facing copy (incl. timeline ` — ` joins) — a real defect." Counter-evidence: UX §7.6's own timeline visual language ships em-dashes ("● Invitation sent — email + SMS"), the export is specified as "a plain-text version (reference, timeline, outcome, signals)" of that timeline, and the RC4.2 on-screen mini-timeline already composes the same join (reference_panel.gleam batch_line: TimelineLine(label <> " — " <> channels, at)) without an em-dash finding in RC4.2 r2. The export's " — " joins are therefore the spec's timeline format in plain text, not an em-dash invented where the spec has none.
detail: Reported for the record per the briefing's explicit timeline-joins category: this is a NEW user-facing composition site in this PR, and a strict reading of the 2026-08-05 ruling ("no em-dash may appear in any landlord-facing copy string") covers the clipboard export. Given §7.6's own format and the accepted RC4.2 precedent, I rate this a note rather than a warning; the round may decide the strict reading applies.
recommended_fix: If the strict ban is to hold everywhere, use plain separators in the export (e.g. " | ") or channel in parentheses; otherwise leave as-is and note the export as spec-format-consistent when consolidating.

title: refcheck_toast_action_failed is defined but never used — the action-error path routes through copy.toast(code, CtxRefcheckAction), so the constant is unreachable dead code
evidence: grep across client/src and client/test for refcheck_toast_action_failed / refcheck_action_failed returns zero usages outside its definition in copy.gleam:890. The error path in client.gleam ApiReturnedRefcheckAction (Error arm, :3538-3545) calls error_toast_copy(err, copy.CtxRefcheckAction) → copy.toast(api_error.code(err), CtxRefcheckAction), which has its own CtxRefcheckAction arms (NotFound :176, Conflict :187, VacancyUnavailable :208, plus the generic fallback) — the constant is never read.
detail: Violates the repo's no-dead-code doctrine (AGENTS.md: "No Technical Debt ... No placeholders, mock functions, TODOs"). The doc comment claims it is the "Action-failure fallback (the api_error copy carries the specific brand line when the server returns one)" — but the fallback for unlisted codes is the generic toast() wildcard arm, making this constant a leftover. Trivial to remove.
recommended_fix: Delete the constant (and its doc comment), or wire it as the CtxRefcheckAction wildcard fallback in copy.toast if the generic copy is not desired for reference actions.
